artifacts.summary: Eight-phase plan landing the Saturation-vs-Completion verdict in the Lean library: bare-relation TaskFrame.Completion, both probes promoted as permanent witnesses, stale open-converse docstrings retired, and the finitary-Completion claim discharged. No manuscript edits.

memory_candidates.content: Frame-constraint separations in the BimodalLogic task-frame development are predicted by how a constraint's quantifier is indexed. A TIME-indexed condition (Completion: a coherent family indexed by a subset X of the temporal order D) collapses to a two-point condition over any order with nearest times, because the constraint imposed by the nearest domain time on each side of the target is the subset-least one. A BALL-indexed condition (Saturation: a supseteq-directed family of fibers and segments) is not indexed by times at all and never collapses, so it can shrink onto a Dedekind cut of the state carrier even when the durations are discrete. Consequence for planning: to separate a time-indexed condition from a ball-indexed one, look at DISCRETE time with an incomplete (dense but non-complete) state carrier; dense time is structurally dead, because over a dense order any coherent family accumulating at a time pinches the witness onto a single real limit. This single distinction underlies three separate results (completion_of_hasNearest, extension_of_isZTime, and the W=Q/D=Z separating frame).
